original_question: Fix any epsilon > 0. Is every monotone Boolean function f : {-1,1}^n -> {-1,1} epsilon-close to a junta whose size is polynomial in deg(f)?
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s exact target. It has the correct quantifier pattern (“fix any ε > 0”), the correct class of functions (monotone Boolean functions f : {-1,1}^n -> {-1,1}), the correct approximation goal (ε-close), the correct target structure (a junta), and the correct governing parameter (deg(f)) with polynomial dependence. In substance, it matches the paper’s stated conjecture almost verbatim.
missing_details: The paper presents this as a named conjecture: the “Servedio–Tan–Verbin Conjecture,” not just as an informal question.
To make the question fully stand-alone, “ε-close” should be defined explicitly, e.g. Pr_x[f(x) != g(x)] <= ε for x uniform on {-1,1}^n.
To make it stand-alone, a “k-junta” should be defined explicitly as a Boolean function depending on at most k coordinates.
To make it stand-alone, “monotone” should be spelled out with respect to the coordinatewise order on {-1,1}^n.
The paper leaves notation implicit; to make the question self-contained, deg(f) should be defined explicitly as the degree of the standard multilinear polynomial representation of f.
The hidden quantifier in “poly(deg(f))” should be made explicit: for each fixed ε, one is asking whether there exists some polynomial p_ε such that every monotone f is ε-close to a p_ε(deg(f))-junta.
If you want the nearby paper context included, the paper notes that one can equivalently replace deg(f) by decision-tree depth or by maximum sensitivity.
For fidelity to the paper’s status note, it should be recorded separately that the paper marks this conjecture as having been resolved negatively by Daniel Kane in 2012.
refined_question: For every fixed ε > 0, does there exist a polynomial p_ε such that every monotone Boolean function f : {-1,1}^n -> {-1,1} is ε-close, with respect to the uniform measure on {-1,1}^n, to a Boolean function g : {-1,1}^n -> {-1,1} that depends on at most p_ε(deg(f)) coordinates, where deg(f) denotes the degree of the standard multilinear polynomial representing f?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, as noted in the paper: for every fixed ε > 0, does there exist a polynomial q_ε such that every monotone Boolean function f : {-1,1}^n -> {-1,1} is ε-close under the uniform measure to a junta depending on at most q_ε(sens[f]) coordinates, where sens[f] is the maximum, over x in {-1,1}^n, of the number of coordinates whose flip changes f(x)?
justification: The draft is aiming at the paper’s standalone problem entry titled “Servedio–Tan–Verbin Conjecture,” whose statement is essentially the same as your sentence. The relevant nearby context in the paper is limited but important: the paper explicitly notes that degree can equivalently be replaced by decision-tree depth or maximum sensitivity, and it also records that the conjecture was later resolved negatively by Daniel Kane. Because the paper explicitly offloads notation and definitions to standard analysis-of-Boolean-functions conventions, a faithful stand-alone rewrite should unpack the meanings of monotone, ε-close, junta, and deg(f), and should make the quantifier hidden in “poly(deg(f))” explicit.
